high.current_state: The fixer's report is correct but understates the problem. The approval row's tenant comes from the ScopeResolver: the user's current_tenant_id, or 'default-tenant' when the user has none and tenancy is not required. The approver's tenant comes from ApprovalManager::tenantOf(), which reads $actor->tenant_id. ApprovalResumer::tenantOf does the same. Neither Telegram (CallbackHandler) nor HTTP (ApprovalController) passes options['tenant_id']. So every accept or reject fails with forbidden unless the actor has both tenant_id and current_tenant_id and they match. Reproduced on the default registry with policy=requester, where the requester accepts their own approval: a plain user gets row 'default-tenant' and forbidden; tenant_id='t1' only gets row 'default-tenant' and forbidden; current_tenant_id='t1' only gets row 't1' and forbidden; a messaging LinkedUser('7','t1') gets row 'default-tenant' and forbidden; both attributes set gives ok.
high.recommended_state: An approver passes the tenant check exactly when the ScopeResolver that stamped the row resolves the approver to the same tenant. Every accept, reject and resume path (HTTP, Telegram, CLI) uses that one rule. A single-tenant host whose User has no tenant attributes can then approve with the default setup.
high.rationale: In a default install, no approval-gated capability can be approved or rejected over Telegram or HTTP. Every tap returns 'You are not allowed to decide this approval.' (after M-202), and the rows sit pending until they expire. It fails closed, so nothing leaks, but the whole D-006 approval loop is unusable unless the host happens to set both attributes. Renaming LinkedUser::$tenantId to tenant_id, as the fixer's note suggests, would not fix it: the row still holds 'default-tenant' or current_tenant_id. Unit tests miss it because every accept test passes an explicit tenant_id option or gives the actor a matching tenant_id (for example l102Approver in ApprovalRetryTest). The fix belongs in core, the messaging sibling only surfaces it. Dedupe with any core finding on ApprovalManager::tenantOf.
high.implementation_hint: Core: inject the bound ScopeResolver (via ResolveTenantFromCaller) into ApprovalManager and ApprovalResumer. Replace tenantOf($actor) with `$this->scopes->resolve(CapabilityContext::make(['caller' => $via, 'actor' => $actor]))->tenantId`, keeping options['tenant_id'] as a trusted override. Delete both tenantOf helpers. Unit tests on the default registry, with no tenant option and no tenant attributes: the requester accepts their own approval (ok), a user with current_tenant_id='t1' accepts a 't1' row (ok) and is refused on a 't2' row (forbidden). Messaging needs no change. Add a CallbackRoutingTest case with a real ApprovalManager and a LinkedUser tapper, which today is forbidden and after the fix is ok.

quick_wins.title: Budget the whole AI turn, not each LLM call, against the claim_ttl job timeout

locations.snippet: $job->timeout = $this->claimTtl; // one job runs the whole turn
while ($rounds < $this->maxToolRounds) { ... $response = $this->llm->complete($messages, $toolDefs);
$started = hrtime(true); // per complete() call, reset every round
return self::elapsedMs($started) + $delayMs + $this->timeoutSeconds * 1000 < $this->deadlineSeconds * 1000;
claim_ttl is also the client's retry deadline, so 429 waits cannot push it past the job.

quick_wins.current_state: RunTurnJob's worker timeout is claim_ttl (120s) for the whole turn, and TurnRunner makes up to max_tool_rounds (8) complete() calls in that one job. The M-104 guard (timeout 110 < claim_ttl 120) and the M-206 retry deadline both measure from the start of each complete() call. So only round 1 is protected. A tool-using turn whose rounds together pass 120s (for example 20s to pick a tool plus a 105s answer, which is under the 110s per-call timeout) or a 429 wait in round 2 gets the worker killed mid-request. The turn then waits for the stale-running reaper.
quick_wins.recommended_state: A turn stops cleanly before it can outlive its job. The runner does not start a new LLM round, and the client does not retry a 429, unless elapsed turn time plus one full request timeout still fits inside claim_ttl minus a small margin. Otherwise the turn fails as a retryable timeout with its progress events, as round-1 timeouts already do.
quick_wins.rationale: M-206 was fixed as specified, but the ContainerBindings and config comments now promise a guarantee that holds for the first round only. Every tool call costs at least a second LLM round, so multi-round turns are the normal agent case, not an edge. A worker killed by the queue timeout also kills the worker process. The user then sees the turn hang until the host-scheduled reaper runs, instead of an immediate retryable error.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Keep the LlmClient contract. Give AnthropicLlmClient an absolute deadline instead of a relative one: `withDeadline(float $monotonicDeadlineMs): self`, or a nullable deadline property. TurnRunner computes `$turnDeadline = hrtime at claim + claimTtl*1000` once. Before each round it fails the turn retryably when `now + timeout*1000 >= turnDeadline`, and it hands the deadline to the client so retryFitsDeadline compares against the turn and not the call. Correct the ContainerBindings and config comments. Unit test with FakeLlmClient and a fake clock: a second round that would start past the budget fails as retryable without calling complete().

enhancements.title: Make the C-202 fix reach warm caches; --no-cache does not refresh them

locations.snippet: cached by an older CLI lack them until the next live describe (`--no-cache`).
if !s.NoCache && s.Cache != nil { if e, ok := s.Cache.Get(name, ""); ok { return e, nil, nil } }
if s.Cache != nil && !s.NoCache { _ = s.Cache.Put(entry) }
sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(c.BaseURL + "\x00" + c.Token))

enhancements.current_state: C-202 added description/readOnly/idempotent to CacheEntry, but describe cache hits have no TTL or version check (service.go:89 calls Get with version ""). So every entry an older CLI cached keeps serving empty fields, and it is refreshed only by `catalog --refresh`, a token change, or a schema rejection. The CHANGELOG tells users to run `--no-cache`, but NoCache skips both the read and the Put (service.go:124). The live describe is shown once and never stored, so the next plain `describe`/`--help` shows no description again.
enhancements.recommended_state: Upgraded installs pick up the new fields with no user action, and the CHANGELOG names a remedy that works.
enhancements.rationale: For anyone who has run a capability before, C-202 is invisible: `describe --json` and `<domain> <verb> --help` still show no description, and those are the agent discovery steps in docs/agents.md. The documented workaround does nothing lasting. Stale readOnly/idempotent read as false because of omitempty, which is the safe direction, so this is low and not a correctness bug.
enhancements.implementation_hint: Version the cache namespace: in PrincipalCache, hash a format tag with the key, e.g. `sha256.Sum256([]byte("v2\x00" + c.BaseURL + "\x00" + c.Token))`. Pre-C-202 entries are then never read, and the first describe refetches. Orphaned old dirs are a few KB under the profile's schemas/ dir. Also change CHANGELOG.md:61 to drop the `--no-cache` advice, or to say `capabilities catalog --refresh` if the version bump is not taken. One catalog unit test: an entry written under the old key is a miss for PrincipalCache.
